interest: Shows careful handling of an interned Japanese diplomat's book, loaned—not seized—to the Library of Congress to preserve his postwar rights.
overview: This file documents the discovery, evaluation, and inter-agency disposition of a Japanese-language reference book—a chronological table of Japanese literature—left at the Greenbrier Hotel in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia, by Tamon Mayeda, former Director of the Japanese Institute in New York City, while interned there with other Japanese diplomats awaiting repatriation in 1942. Transmitted to Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr. by FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover, the scholarly volume was reviewed by the State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs and Special Division. To avoid complications with enemy property custodianship and ensure the book could be returned to Maeda without embarrassment after the war, the Department arranged to deposit the book with the Library of Congress on an indefinite loan for safe-keeping, which the Library formally acknowledged in September 1942.
